A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same survey. Their main texts, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable, including architecture material moved from v5 Section 3.1.1 to v6 Appendix C.

before.justification: Figure 5 reports annual publication counts derived from the authors' collected literature. This constitutes original descriptive data analysis, although v5 reports no original solver experiments.

after.justification: Figure 5 retains and updates the survey's original publication-count analysis. The new performance Table 1 separately attributes its model scores to the original papers, rather than reporting new experiments.

M1.justification: Neither version introduces a solver algorithm or model. The reviewed architecture and training-method taxonomy remains stable; the geometry-specific reinforcement-learning suggestions are future directions, not implemented method changes.

E1.justification: The appendix dataset catalogues retain the same coverage after matching Tangram/GeoER, GeoPeP/GeoMetric and MathGlance/MatheMetric. The new performance table summarizes already-reviewed benchmarks without adding original training or evaluation scenarios.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates baselines against a proposed solver. The eight models in v6 Table 1 form a literature-sourced performance summary, not a newly conducted baseline experiment.

E3.justification: The literature-search procedure and corresponding appendix dataset splits and sizes remain unchanged. Section 4 reorganizes descriptions of evaluation methods, but no actual experimental protocol change is documented.

E4.justification: No original ablations, sensitivity tests, robustness experiments or case studies are added or removed. Section 5.1 adds benchmark synthesis and interpretation rather than supplementary experimental analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version supplies repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests for its analyses. The new performance table reports individual scores without uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: V6 adds the first quantitative performance table across eight models and three benchmarks, including LANS at 82.3 on Geometry3K-test and URSA-8B at 83.2 on MathVista-testmini-GPS. These are newly reported literature-sourced results, not version-to-version performance gains. Figure 5 also changes the 2024 and 2025 counts from 111 and 84 to 112 and 83.

T1.justification: No mathematical assumptions, theorems, derivations or proofs are introduced or revised. The illustrative geometry proof in Figure 3 is unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion newly identify representative-model performance analysis as a survey contribution. The central task, method and evaluation survey claims remain intact.

C2.justification: New Section 5.1 interprets performance through reinforcement learning, neural-symbolic methods, training data and test-time scaling, adding benchmark-saturation and deployment concerns. Sections 5.2–5.3 substantially extend discussion of efficiency tradeoffs and geometry-specific rewards. Conversely, the earlier explicit caution about LLM-judge hallucinations is removed.

D1.justification: V6 updates the MathGlance/MatheMetric dataset resource link and trims component-level descriptions of hybrid systems such as Pi-GPS in Section 3.1.2. Most encoder-decoder details are preserved through relocation to Appendix C, rather than newly disclosed.

R1.justification: V6 adds Liu et al. (2019a)'s AIFU system and stronger historical neural-symbolic framing, while removing several general references, including Sun et al. (2023) and Kurisappan and Pandiya (2025). Most other bibliography changes update publication metadata or titles of retained works.

P1.justification: Sections 1–5 are extensively rewritten and condensed. Detailed architecture coverage moves to Appendix C, Section 4 becomes automatic versus manual evaluation, and Section 5 gains a performance-analysis subsection and a separate reinforcement-learning direction.

P2.justification: V6 adds performance Table 1, redraws Figure 1 to reflect the revised organization, and relocates Figures 2–3. Existing dataset and architecture tables retain their column structures, with renamed or reordered entries; the overall two-column design remains.

improvement.justification: The condensed main narrative, preserved architecture details in Appendix C, and new performance and efficiency discussion make v6 more useful as a survey. These gains are limited by the loss of practical evaluation detail in Section 4 and by Table 1's lack of documented harmonization across its literature-sourced scores.
